## Natural history notes

A small yellow butterfly characterized by bright lemon-yellow wings, narrow dark borders on the upperside, and faint brownish markings on the underside that help distinguish it from similar sulphurs. In Florida, it is common in sunny open habitats such as fields, prairies, roadsides, gardens, lawns, pine flatwoods, and disturbed areas where low legumes are present. Adults feed on nectar from small flowers, while the caterpillars feed mainly on plants in the pea family, especially partridge pea and related low-growing legumes.
